name: Heroism and the heroic code
description: The ethic of the Germanic warrior: courage in the face of doom, the pursuit of fame (lof), and the obligations of honour.

name: Wyrd (fate) and providence
description: The interplay of inexorable fate (wyrd) with the Christian understanding of divine providence, pervasive in Old English poetry.

name: Exile and homelessness
description: The state of the wanderer cut off from lord, hall, and kin; the defining condition of the Old English elegies.

name: The transience of earthly glory (ubi sunt)
description: Meditation on the ruin of halls and kingdoms and the brevity of all worldly splendour ('where are they now?').

name: Sea voyage and seafaring
description: The sea as literal hardship, allegory of the soul's pilgrimage, and landscape of spiritual testing.

name: Loyalty and the comitatus bond
description: The reciprocal bond between lord and retainer: protection and gift-giving in exchange for service unto death.

name: Kingship and good rule
description: The ideal of the just king as ring-giver and protector of his people, contrasted with tyrants and failing rulers.

name: Treasure, gift-giving, and reciprocity
description: Gold, rings, and weapons as tokens of the social bond and as emblems of earthly vanity; the hoard and its futility.

name: Blood-feud, vengeance, and kinship
description: The obligations and disasters of the feud, the claims of kin, and the tragic cost of revenge.

name: Christian-pagan synthesis
description: The coexistence and fusion of Germanic heroic values with Christian teaching in the literature of conversion-age England.

name: Death, the soul, and the afterlife
description: The fate of the soul after death, the dialogue of soul and body, and the soul's reckoning.

name: Judgment Day and eschatology
description: The Last Judgment, the end of the world, and the homiletic urgency of repentance.

name: Wisdom and learning
description: The value of knowledge, counsel, and education, from gnomic maxims to the Alfredian program of translation.

name: Creation and cosmology
description: The created order as the book of God: the wonder of the world, the phoenix, the sea, and the heavens.

name: Typology and biblical interpretation
description: The reading of Old Testament figures and events as prefigurations of Christ and the Church.

name: Consolation and endurance
description: The wisdom of bearing suffering patiently, whether the wanderer's exile or the martyr's trial.

name: Warfare and battle
description: The conduct and commemoration of war, from heroic single combat to the national battles of the tenth century.

name: Solitude and the hall community
description: The contrast between the warmth and order of the hall and the loneliness of the exile or hermit.

name: Women's experience and the feminine voice
description: The rare but powerful voices of women in the poetry: the lamenting wife, Judith, Juliana, Elene.

name: Mission, conversion, and the Church
description: The spread of Christianity, the work of missionaries, and the life of the institutional Church.

name: Monsters and the marvellous
description: Grendel and the dragon, the wonders of the East, and the Christian allegorization of fabulous beasts.
